name: http_request
description: Make HTTP requests to external APIs - one attempt; the status and body come back as the result, a network failure as an error

body_data.description: Request body as object (auto-stringified to JSON). Use instead of body for structured data; string values may be templates over the read view (@input, @result.<node>).

name: knowledge_search
description: Search the organization's knowledge bases: the hits (content, score, sourceType; term and synonyms for terminology; metadata, with a table's row as metadata.row) are the output, best first. The query is split at commas, semicolons, newlines and 'and' into items searched in parallel; exactKey instead finds one key exactly, with no model and no similar match. No hits is a success with an empty output.

query.description: What to look up, in a few words. Required unless exactKey is given.

exactKey.description: One key to find exactly, in place of a search: a table row's term or synonym, with no model and no similar match

keyColumn.description: With exactKey: the header of the table column the key is in

knowledgeBaseIds.description: Restrict the search to these knowledge bases; empty searches all of the organization's

sourceType.description: Which kind of knowledge to search; absent searches both

name: org_directory
description: List the organization's members as callable targets. Each entry has an identifier (user:<id>) directly usable as an invoke-node call target or transfer destination, plus name, username, email and organization roles. Use to decide WHO to call/consult dynamically.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive filter matched against name, username, email and role names (a role or a person's name)

name: web_search
description: Search the web and answer briefly with sources: current events, facts, weather, opening hours, places. Use instead of guessing whenever the question is about the outside world. A place the answer depends on must be in the query.

query.description: The question in the person's own words, including any place it is about.

name: brain_lookup
description: Read one thing from the company brain by its key, with no model and no search: its entity and its current properties as {property: value}, who asserted each and when. By source + externalId (the key a system knows it by), or by type + name (the exact name; a name that fits several answers ambiguous with the candidates and picks none). `where` narrows a key or name to a property's value, and with no key lists the things holding that value. Nothing found is a success with found false. People are not records.

source.description: The system the key belongs to

externalId.description: The thing's key in that system, exactly as it knows it

type.description: What kind of thing it is, with name or where

where.description: One property's value it must hold: { property, value }

limit.description: How many things at most, when several hold the value

name: brain_set
description: Write one value of one thing in the company brain by its key, with no model: the property holds this value from now on, the value before stays as history unless the property is live state, which keeps its latest value only. A value of the wrong datatype is refused and nothing is written. The fact is marked as written by this flow, with the person in the conversation as its observer. In a conversation driven through /dev it answers as written and writes nothing, unless the caller sends X-Dev-Memory: on. People are not records.

source.description: The system the key belongs to

externalId.description: The thing's key in that system, exactly as it knows it

property.description: Which of its properties to set

value.description: The value: one text, number or true/false

type.description: What kind of thing it is, for a key nobody knows yet

name.description: What to call it, for a key nobody knows yet; default: the key

name: find_colleague
description: Find the colleagues best placed to help with a problem, from the company brain: who holds a role, has a skill, is responsible for a thing, or has been consulted about similar matters — presence-aware. Returns ranked candidates, each with a reason and an identifier (user:<id>) usable as an invoke-node call target or a handoff destination, plus `suggested` (the top candidate). Use when the flow lets the assistant decide WHO to bring in; prefer a fixed rule on the invoke node (role:…, responsible_for:…) when the organization's policy already says who.

problem.description: What needs solving, in the user's words — matched against what the organization knows about people

role.description: Narrow to people holding this role

skill.description: Narrow to people with this skill

responsibleFor.description: Narrow to people responsible for this thing (an asset, an area, a process)

team.description: Narrow to members of this team

name: send_message
description: Send a message on another channel (SMS or WhatsApp) to a recipient WITHOUT interrupting the current conversation. Fire-and-forget; a reply comes back as a separate session. Use when the useful thing to hand the user is a link, code, or address they cannot act on by voice.

target.description: Recipient address (phone number for sms/whatsapp): the number the conversation or a flow input names - never guessed.
